events.title: A new particle is found
events.description: CERN reports a particle consistent with the long-sought Higgs boson.

events.title: A spacecraft visits Pluto
events.description: New Horizons makes a close flyby after a journey of billions of miles.

events.title: UK voters choose to leave the EU
events.description: The referendum result begins a long process of leaving the European Union.

what_happened_next.text:
Amazon grew to more than four times its starting value. The US share basket and Apple both gained roughly 85–90%, while Exxon Mobil gained much less. A successful product or a profitable year did not tell you which investment would grow fastest over the next five years.

The hunt for the Higgs boson was still in the news when you began. In July 2012, CERN reported a particle consistent with it. New Horizons reached Pluto in 2015, and UK voters chose to leave the European Union in 2016. The future brought answers to some questions and entirely new questions to others.

Amazon’s gain stands out, but it was one company among many. The US share basket also grew strongly without requiring an investor to identify that exact winner. Exxon Mobil remained a large business, yet its share return was much smaller. Company size, useful products and an investment’s growth are related ideas, but they are not the same measurement.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The election, housing, oil prices and new technology drew attention. Scientists were still searching for the Higgs boson.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: Companies followed different paths. Spreading money across many businesses meant relying less on any single product, oil price or company.
reflection.what_faded_away: A record sales announcement was useful information about the past. It was not a promise of the same growth every year.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The future ranking was unknown. Amazon’s large gain looks obvious on the finished chart, but it was not printed in the starting news.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: Apple kept turning its large customer base into sales of iPhones, Macs, watches and services. The holiday quarter ended December 2016 brought record revenue of $78.4 billion, with records across those product groups. Apple also paid cash to shareholders and bought back some of its shares. The investment grew, although product sales did not rise smoothly every quarter.

Amazon’s growth came from more than shopping. Its Amazon Web Services business sold computing power to other companies and became a major source of profit. In 2016, AWS earned $3.1 billion before company-wide costs, while Amazon’s total annual sales reached $136 billion. Prime and online shopping also expanded. The company was beginning to turn years of investment into much larger earnings.

Low oil and gas prices squeezed ExxonMobil’s earnings during the later part of this period. In 2016 it earned $7.8 billion, less than half its 2015 profit. That included a roughly $2 billion cut to the value of gas assets. Continued dividends helped the investment finish slightly ahead, but weak energy profits limited the reward from holding the shares.
